# Sync hub and relay

The sync hub lets several people share staff and project work. Your organization runs it itself, as a container. The relay is a separate small service for chats that arrive from outside the editor; today it is only a foundation and carries no messages yet. Both are built into minimal images with no shell or package manager.

Back to the [component catalogue](./index.md).

## npm:jose

**What it provides.** Signs and verifies the relay's JSON Web Tokens; bundled into the relay image.

**Why it is needed.** The relay's planned library for signing and verifying its JSON Web Tokens, and its only runtime dependency: the relay workspace test (relay/test/workspace.test.ts) requires exactly this dependency. No relay source imports it yet; the relay channel phases are the first to use it, for token checks. Without it the relay would need its own JWT code.

## image:docker.io/bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api

**What it provides.** Optional Signal sidecar for the relay (Compose profile "signal", off by default); it relays messages through the Signal service.

**Why it is needed.** The planned Signal channel sidecar for the relay (Phase 82). It is off by default and is not started until Phase 82 re-pins it to a current release and re-reviews this entry; the relay does not send or receive Signal messages yet. Without it the relay would need its own Signal client.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | Container image |
| Pinned version or digest | `0.101@sha256:2cf09d66a86fdd210e42ee91662216364acc27da1163a8c44167a77ea3a6559a` |

| Used in | `relay/compose.yaml` |

| Cryptography | Not a validated cryptographic module |
| Air gap | Needs the internet: does not work air-gapped |
| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |
| Controls | AC-20, SA-9, SC-7, SC-13, SR-3 |
| Security fixes | Third-party single-maintainer image pinned by digest; not scanned in CI. signal-cli stops working about three months after release, so the pin lapses about 2026-12-10 (owner decision 2026-11-18: left to lapse until Phase 82). |
| Reviewed | Claude (agent review; owner to confirm), 2026-11-23 |

Conditions:

- Off by default; do not start the "signal" profile until Phase 82 re-pins it to a current release and re-reviews this entry.
- It sends messages through the Signal service on the public internet (a commercial service outside your organization): use it only where your organization's policy allows, and never for Protected B, Controlled Goods or ITAR information.
- It cannot work at an air-gapped site.
- Its cryptography (the Signal protocol in signal-cli) is not a FIPS 140 validated module.
- Add it to the image vulnerability scan before it is first used.

## image:gcr.io/distroless/nodejs26-debian13

**What it provides.** Final base image of the relay and hub: Node 26 as a non-root user, with no shell or package manager.

**Why it is needed.** The final, minimal base of the relay and hub images: Node.js as a non-root user, with no shell or package manager. This removes most of the attack surface a full operating system image would add.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | Container image |
| Pinned version or digest | `nonroot@sha256:ffa8a7545403036c94ec76674b5dbac2d425af2d679147cdf3e30180071487b7` |
| Architecture component | `relay` |
| Used in | `hub/Dockerfile`, `relay/Dockerfile` |
| Scope | Runtime: it runs in the product |
| Licence | Apache-2.0 (distroless); Node.js MIT and Debian packages under their own licences |
| Cryptography | Not a validated cryptographic module |
| Air gap | Works air-gapped once mirrored: the pinned gcr.io/distroless/nodejs26-debian13 digest in a local registry |
| Compliance fit | Pass with conditions |
| Controls | CM-2, CM-7, SC-13, SI-2, SR-3, SR-11 |
| Security fixes | grype scans the built relay image in the relay-image-scan CI job and fails it on a high fixed vulnerability (a reporting job, not a required check); the digest is re-pinned by hand when Google publishes a fixed image. |
| Reviewed | Claude (agent review; owner to confirm), 2026-11-24 |

Conditions:

- Air-gapped and on-premise sites must mirror this exact digest into a local registry (gcr.io is a commercial-cloud registry).
- The hub's TLS and the relay's token signing run on the Node.js OpenSSL in this image, which is not a FIPS 140 validated module (gap X8): a Protected B deployment needs its authorizing official to accept the comparable-strength basis, or a validated provider.
- Act on the relay-image-scan result before each release; it does not block a merge.
- Protected B needs a UBI 9 base with the OpenSSL FIPS provider on a FIPS host; the rebase is coordinated with Phase 46 (P11, one Node major).
- On-premise, the hub runs on Kubernetes, several per site, each from the published, signed digest (D-45, D-46).
